chunks: Muhammad ibn Ya'qub from a number of our companions from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from Sa'd ibn Abi Khalaf said:

I asked Abu al-Hasan Musa (peace be upon him) about the man who is 'sarurah' (unable to perform Hajj himself), does he perform Hajj on behalf of the deceased? He said: 'Yes, if the sarurah does not have what he needs to perform Hajj for himself. But if he has what he needs to perform Hajj for himself, then it is not sufficient for the deceased until he performs Hajj from his own wealth. And she (the deceased) is sufficient for the deceased if the sarurah has wealth, and if he does not have wealth.'

key_terms.الصَّرُورَةُ: A person who is unable to perform Hajj for themselves due to lack of means or ability
key_terms.يَحُجُّ عَنِ الْمَيِّتِ: Performs Hajj on behalf of the deceased
key_terms.يُجْزِي: Is sufficient/valid (as a discharge of obligation)

ai.seo_question: What is the condition for a person unable to perform Hajj themselves to perform Hajj on behalf of the deceased?
ai.summary: This narration from Imam Musa al-Kazim (AS) clarifies the priority of the obligatory Hajj (Fard) over the voluntary or representative Hajj (Nafl/Ta'abbudi) for a 'sarurah' (one capable but not yet obligated). It establishes that wealth sufficiency for one's own Hajj is a prerequisite for validity when performing on behalf of another, ensuring the individual's primary religious duty is fulfilled first. This ruling highlights the Shia jurisprudential principle that representative acts of worship are contingent upon the completion or sufficiency of the performer's own obligatory duties.
